system.name: T-REGS
system.one_liner: A regulariser for joint-embedding self-supervised learning that maximises the minimum-spanning-tree length of each branch's embeddings, with a sphere constraint, to avoid collapse and spread points uniformly.
domain: minimum spanning tree on a hypersphere

content.variant_note: two view branches run into one embedding sphere where three loss terms are drawn as three line styles, with a second sphere showing the outcome
content.argues: Aligning the two views while pushing apart the edge-connected points of each branch's spanning tree, on a sphere, yields uniformly distributed aligned embeddings without dimensional collapse.
content.subject: Twin augmented-view branches through a shared encoder and projector into embeddings on a hypersphere, with MST edges and three loss terms, then the resulting uniform configuration.

new_tags.name: loss-glyph-legend
new_tags.what: legend rows pair a line style or arrowhead used on the drawing with the loss term it stands for, terms coloured like the elements they act on

lessons.what_to_learn: Key each loss term by a distinct line or arrowhead style (gradient line = align, bow-tie = repel, dotted = constrain) drawn identically on the embedding picture and in the legend, with the formula term coloured by the view it acts on; repeat the same space at the end state beside it.
lessons.suits: Regularisers or objectives that act geometrically on embeddings (alignment, repulsion, uniformity, constraints) in SSL, metric learning or representation analysis.

evidence: Two augmented views X, X′ are encoded by fθ and projected by hϕ into embeddings Z, Z′.
maximizes the minimum-spanning-tree length on each branch, LE(Z) and LE(Z′), repelling edge-connected points
As a result, T-REGS induces uniformly distributed embeddings without dimensional collapse.

summary: T-REGS is a regularisation framework for joint-embedding self-supervised learning that maximises the length of a minimum spanning tree over each branch's embeddings, together with a sphere constraint, to prevent dimensional collapse and promote uniformity. Figure 1 shows two augmented views of an image flowing through a shared encoder f and projector h (grey trapezoids) into embeddings Z and Z', drawn as orange and blue points on a wireframe sphere. Three line styles tie the loss terms to the picture: a gradient line aligns paired views, bow-tie arrowheads on the tree edges push points apart, dotted lines hold points on the sphere. A second sphere shows the outcome: aligned pairs spread evenly.
summary_zh: T-REGS 用最小生成树长度做自监督正则。图1左侧：两个增广视图经共享的编码器 f 与投影头 h 得到嵌入，画成球面上的橙、蓝点；三种线型对应三项损失；右侧球面展示结果：成对点对齐且均匀分布。
